For the unit-vertex octahedron O and Haar plane H=u^perp, intrinsic polarity gives (O∩H)^polar,H=P_H([-1,1]^3), so the centered disk inradius obeys R^{-2}=max_{eps∈{±1}³}||P_H eps||²=3-min_eps(eps·u)². Sorting |u| as a>=b>=c reduces the minimal signed sum to |a-b-c|, including the q<0 spherical chamber. Its range [-1/sqrt(3),1] establishes support [1/sqrt(3),1/sqrt(2)]. The q>t event is the 24 sign/order copies of x>y+z+t; direct polar-coordinate spherical area integration reproduces P_+(t). The q<-t event is eight congruent small-circle spherical triangles; Gauss–Bonnet gives P_-(t) with cut-off t_c=1/sqrt(3). The collapsing spherical triangle has area (9sqrt(3)/8)(t_c-t)^2+O((t_c-t)^3); because t(r*)=t_c and t'(r*)=16sqrt(2)/3, the left-minus-right second-derivative jump is -256sqrt(3)/pi, first derivatives matching. Independently evaluated the positive-tail spherical integral at seven thresholds t=0,.2,.4,1/sqrt(3),.65,.9,1 with scipy quadrature against the claimed closed formula (agreement at floating-point rounding), checked endpoint tails sum to one; inspected the distinct vertex/edge geometric section inradius verifier. Continuum differentiability comes from the geometric asymptotics, not these finite checks.
